name: Book Launch: The New Science of Living Longer and Better
content:
B&N .com BESTSELLER

CHEATING DEATH: The New Science of Living Longer and Better

I trust this finds you well and continuing to optimize your health. To that end, I’m letting you know that my book, Cheating Death, The New Science of Living Longer and Better, was released March 7, 2023, and is now available for purchase. For Regenerative & Sports Medicine patients, when you purchase Cheating Death from this site, you will receive one (1) complimentary 2-day shipping on your next medication order.

Since I am frequently asked, “What else can I do to optimize my health?”, and we are invariably limited by consultation time, I decided to present the answers to this question in book form so it is both informative and useful. My goal is that it sparks further conversation between you and me about what’s possible when it comes to improving your healthspan and longevity outlook.

You can obtain a copy by visiting www.CheatingDeath.com, and, as my way of saying thank you for your support during this book launch, Regenerative & Sports Medicine will not only provide you one (1) complimentary 2-day shipping on your next refill but also early access to my new app, “Death Clock,” and, you will be among the first to receive episodes one, two, and three of my new docuseries, Beyond Genetics.

This informative if impractical debut by physician McClain explores medical treatments that promise to help patients “live longer, heal faster, and feel better.” He makes the standard case for eating right, exercising, and sleeping well, but the juiciest recommendations are the most futuristic. The author touts the promise of stem cell treatments for restoring damaged tissue and surveys the different types of stem cells, noting that somatic stem cells “replace or repair” specific kinds of cells while pluripotent cells can transform into any kind. Scientific explanations back up his suggestions, though readers might struggle to follow the jargon, such as McClain’s contention that cryotherapy increases longevity “by reducing free radicals, increasing cellular respiration and thermogenesis.” However, the author is careful not to oversell experimental therapies and cautions that while gene editing has shown promise in treating cancer and muscular dystrophy, it’s “still in a developmental phase” and scientists haven’t figured out how to prevent gene changes from “crossing over” into cells scientists didn’t intend to alter. Suggestions to get one’s genome sequenced and stem cells banked, meanwhile, don’t address the prohibitive costs of these technologies. Nonetheless, this serves as a solid overview of pioneering treatments and makes for a stimulating glimpse into what the future of aging might look like.

Best,

Rand McClain, D.O.
Regenerative & Sports Medicine

name: March 2023 Newsletter
content:
I would like to provide a few updates and opportunities to promote healthspan focusing on fat loss.

Many are asking about the latest drug, branded as Wegovy, being touted as the first ever FDA-approved for weight loss (“chronic weight management in adults with obesity”). The drug, a GLP-1 agonist generically named, semaglutide, and also branded as Ozempic and similar to another drug, tirzepatide, and branded as Mounjaro, is an injectable medication administered just under the skin weekly has been shown to reduce body weight very significantly without much effort. Semaglutide was approved for treatment of diabetes in 2017 and therefore has an established record of use that includes safety, efficacy, and few potential side effects. I have begun prescribing semaglutide for diabetes and weight loss since the beginning of 2022, and have witnessed considerable improvements in health with its use with the only noted side effect being some nausea if one started at too high a dose or advanced the dosing too quickly.

Because of its success as an effective weight loss tool, there is a Nationwide shortage of the brand-named drugs. Even where available, the brands are quite expensive. Our compounder, Empower Pharmacy, provides semaglutide at less than $100/month. Anyone interested in a trial of semaglutide for weight loss or to replace existing blood sugar lowering medications is welcome to contact us to consider starting a course of semaglutide treatment.

App Release

For those interested in determining where one stands in terms of “Biological Age” (BA) versus “Chronological Age”(CA), with the help of a team of very bright mathematicians, programmers and developers, I have developed an App, “The Death Clock” to help not only determine one’s effective real age, but to measure the differences made to one’s BA as a result of changes made to one’s life – including medical, supplemental, exercise, nutrition, sleep and other modifiable factors and interventions – to improve one’s healthspan (healthy longevity).

We are simply waiting for Apple’s final approval before you will see it available for download from the Apple App store, literally any day now. Within the App (but also directly through our office, if you prefer) one can enter data linked to BA and healthspan ranging from basic demographics and history, to laboratory assays, to more extensive testing and evaluations including telomere length and DNA methylation measurements.

With regards to healthy nutrition as well as efforts toward fat loss, not included in my book, but for those who ask about these food options, we have finally launched our first offering – a “Coconut Cashew” bar - in the nutritional food space using the functional sweetener, allulose. Our brand is called, Taste and Bliss, and we will follow this initial offering with more bars as well as drink mixes similar to “Crystal Light” but containing not only allulose but additional nutritious ingredients designed to optimize cognition and activation of the parasympathetic nervous system (the calming state that promotes regeneration).

Hindsight on COVID:

Of note recently is an article published in the British medical journal, The Lancet, that provides a systematic review and meta-analysis of 65 studies from 19 different countries demonstrating that those with natural immunity to COVID conferred by infection with the SARS CoV-2 virus had equal immunity and protection against reinfection equal to those vaccinated with two doses of the mRNA COVID vaccines. Good news for those previously infected with the virus as well as some vindication for those who drafted the Great Barrington Declaration and perhaps enough evidence to stifle mandates to be vaccinated if one has already been infected.

Lastly, I would like to remind you that my book, Cheating Death, The New Science of Living Longer and Better was released March 7th and is now available for purchase. Thank you to those who have already purchased a copy and contributed to its “Best Seller” status in Barnes and Noble and Amazon stores. I hope its contents will be informative and useful, and will promote conversation in our future consultations and communications about the opportunities we have available to increase our healthspan.

Best in health,

Rand McClain, D.O.

name: November 2022 Newsletter
content:
NOVEMBER NEWSLETTER

I trust this finds you all in great health and getting even better. In the interest of continually optimizing health and I’m writing with some updates.

Good news! A recently produced “Findings of Fact and Conclusions of Law” issued by the United States District, Central District of California – Eastern Division essentially makes the use of human stem cells legal in the U.S. by disagreeing with the FDA’s position to classify stem cells as a drug which then requires significant testing, time and expense through clinical trials and approval by the FDA before they can be used for medical treatment of humans. The FDA has missed its window of opportunity to appeal the decision. Thus, doctors can now use stem cells to treat patients for a myriad of applicable conditions and per the doctor’s discretion.

VIEW FINDINGS

As a source for evaluation and some more motivation, I ask and encourage all of you to join my portal within Garmin Connect, an application that collects exercise data and aggregates it in an easy way to assess and evaluate effort, progress and fitness. Simply sign up for a free account at connect.garmin.com and search for me: Rand McClain, Malibu, CA, click on “Connect” and as soon as I get the request, I’ll complete the connection. I will be able to see any workouts/exercise you post, and you will have access to mine as well. No others will be able to see your workouts unless you specifically connect with them in the same way you do with me. While you (or I) won’t receive a free toaster or anything from Garmin, sharing data with each other will enable us to more precisely evaluate progress toward fitness goals plus it can just be fun sharing and “keeping each other honest” – like training partners.

SIGN UP

HYDRATION & SWEAT

Although it looks like it may be the last of it for this year in the northern hemisphere, a quick note about heat and the “masters” athlete. When we are young, the sweat produced to reduce core body heat is limited naturally and physiologically at some point to avoid dehydration though at the added secondary risk of raising body temperature. I can remember trying to cut weight for wrestling matches in high school and eventually – by the third trip into the sauna – just getting hot and not sweating at all.

As we age, that mechanism fails and the body does not limit the amount of water lost in an effort to dissipate heat. The result can be catastrophic leading to heat exhaustion or heat stroke – especially if you remember your youth and having successfully navigated the heat without the slightest issue. For us “masters” athletes it is imperative that we give extra consideration to hydration and awareness to external (as well as internal) temperatures while training. There is no set amount of liquid required – the proper amount will be a factor of temperature, output/intensity, fitness, age and, as always, individual requirements, but weighing before and after exercise (as a gauge of water loss) and hydrating at regular intervals is a good start to finding out what works best for you. Also, if you are training in heat frequently, you may find it valuable (as I have) to invest in a CORE sensor to monitor your body temperature while exercising.

LEARN MORE ABOUT CORE SENSOR

For those of you who have not heard about allulose, it is a non-caloric functional sweetener that is actually naturally produced (as opposed to an “artificial sweetener”). It has been shown in some studies to actually reduce blood glucose (“sugar”) and looks, feels and tastes like real table sugar. It can be used to cook and in a ratio of 1:1.5 matches sugar sweetness and other functionality (except for calories) almost exactly. You can find this molecule online, but few, if any, products made with allulose. So, I have begun manufacturing bars and drink mixes using this healthy functional sweetener and hope to have them packaged and ready to go by the end of this year.

STEM CELL SKIN CARE

We are also preparing to launch a suite of stem cell-based topical formulations for the skin to include different concentrations for the around the eyes, face and body. We hope to announce availability by the first quarter next year. These products mimic the results of the Personal Cell Science line that we still offer but using umbilical cord tissue cells and thereby obviating the need to harvest one’s own cells.

OUR OFFICE ANNOUNCEMENTS

We have recently (August 5th) opened our Houston office with Dr. Todd acting as its Medical Director and primary provider. As many of you know Dr. Todd comes to us from Baylor University’s urology program headed by Dr. Larry Lipshultz, and Dr. Todd will be adding testosterone pellet implantation to the list of TRT offerings RSM provides.

We are also opening our service throughout the country of Canada. Dr. Norry Kaler will oversee operations there as our Medical Director. We look forward to being able to help optimize health in Canada and expanding to the United Kingdom and Australia.

VISIT OUR WEBSITE

This year we celebrate the 3-year anniversaries of three of our RSM Team members, Holli (Pockets) Bell, Jamie and Kira. For those of you still with us from the earlier years, you are well aware of the blessing we have in these three individuals working with RSM instead of predecessors!

For those interested in furthering their fitness goals, please visit MindPump. These gentlemen have the requisite knowledge of human physiology and exercise movements and techniques to help achieve the body composition and fitness level desired by anyone interested. We participate together in a FB forum and with occasional podcasts that summarize some of the concepts of health optimization.

VISIT MINDPUMP

Walter Reed Army Medical Center and American Cryostem (“CRYO”) have entered into an agreement to study the effects and treatment of “Long COVID” (persistent and often debilitating symptoms after SARS-CoV-2 infection). I will be participating as a sub-investigator in these studies and the results should help provide access to stem cell treatment for Long COVID. Meanwhile, we are approximately halfway through our study treating Post-Concussion Syndrome with autologous stem cells and the results are so far outstanding and provide further proof of stem cells efficacy in treating Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI).

NEUROMUSCULAR THERAPY

Lastly, for anyone in Los Angeles in need of Neuromuscular Therapy (aka massage or bodywork), our Manhattan Beach location provides treatment 7 days a week. If you would prefer treatment at home, I have yet to find a better masseur than Weitao "Jason" Zhang at (626) 550-6722. Without reservation, I encourage anyone interested in recovery from injury or simply from weekly exercise to take advantage of Jason’s expertise. Without his help, personally, I would not have so quickly recovered so successfully and quickly from two hip replacement surgeries last year, and he has since kept me in top form.‬‬

Best in health,

Rand

name: November 2023 Newsletter: Updates on Peptides, Rapamycin & Healthspan
content:
I trust this finds you well and consistently making gains toward improving your healthspan. I would like to share some recent developments in regenerative medicine that deserve some attention, and, I would like to share my opinion with you regarding efforts to optimize your healthspan.

The FDA has recently decided that many of the popular peptides (CJC-1295, Ipamorelin, BPC-157, AOD 9604, and Kisspeptin) and peptidomimetics (ibutamoren) are not safe for human use and has restricted their availability (read: made illegal except for officially recognized research purposes). Unfortunately, this will remove many useful tools we have had available to us to treat a multitude of ailments and injuries quite safely to date. I will keep you posted with any changes to regulation of as well as alternatives to these medical treatments.

Rapamycin

Meanwhile, a drug typically used to prevent rejection of transplanted organs and some cancers, Rapamycin, is gaining more and more attention as a potentially powerful tool to increase healthspan through its ability to initiate autophagy and cellular regeneration by antagonizing mTORC1.

In plain speak, this means that proper use of rapamycin shows effectiveness in helping the cell “clean up the mess” and “recycle” certain valuable contents.

Analogous to a busy restaurant kitchen, in order to continue producing fresh, uncontaminated and properly cooked dishes, during autophagy, resources are temporarily shifted to emphasize cleaning the pots and pans, the countertops and even the splattering’s on the recipe book (cellular DNA) that, eg, make it hard to determine if the quantity referenced in the recipe is an “8” or a “3”.

This process also disposes of “spoiled” ingredients while “recycling” valuable, still fresh and useful ones. This process helps preserve the proper function of the cell so that it is still producing tasty dishes according to recipe instead of producing altered and/or contaminated dishes. This is important not only for the obvious reasons, but also because, to change analogies, just like an untuned vehicle can pollute the air around it, so can an “untuned” (aka “senescent”) cell contaminate and disrupt function of surrounding, otherwise healthy cells.

Good news!


EXERCISE… in sufficient quantity and intensity (different for each individual) can effectuate similar effects to rapamycin! So, while it appears that rapamycin, by antagonizing (turning off) mTORC1, will provide some additive effects to the ability of exercise to initiate autophagy, exercise can provide sufficient effects without having to negate some of the beneficial effects (like skeletal muscle growth and improved brain function) that mTORC1 can provide.

BOTTOM LINE: Keep up with your exercise routine as one of your greatest sources of health optimization!

Along these lines, many have been asking about supplementing with nicotinamide riboside (NR) or nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) as a source of NAD+ generation that, through different mechanisms of action (e.g., AMPK and SIRT1 and SIRT3 gene activation), effectuate the same desired results mentioned above, including autophagy.

The best source for generating NAD+? EXERCISE! So, most of you can save your money for other beneficial supplements while generating plenty of NAD+ with your daily exercise complement.

For those of you interested in either a more rigorous approach to improving your healthspan or who simply would like to enjoy more attention to details on a regular basis, RSM is now offering two new programs to facilitate both.

Concierge II:

For those interested in more frequent and comprehensive evaluation of their progress toward healthspan optimization and quick access to RSM services including communication with our providers, scheduling of appointments and facilitation of prescription and supplements refills as well as diagnostic procedures.

Concierge I:

For those interested in the most complete workup and evaluation of one’s current health, and development of a comprehensive treatment plan designed to optimize healthspan with one’s individual goals in mind along with consistent monitoring of progress and commensurate changes in action plan.

Included are diagnostic imaging and laboratory assays as part of annual screening for cardiovascular health, cancer, neurological disorders, and metabolic function (the four major causes of morbidity and mortality in Western culture) as well as estimates of biological (versus chronological) age and rate of aging. Comprehensive and specific interventional treatments and actionable plans for healthspan optimization are provided based upon results of serial testing and clinical observation of progress toward individual goals.

A word about informational sources on the internet, Instagram and Facebook (et al): I am sure it is apparent that many laypeople –including those with a lack of proper education and/or knowledge of human physiology, lack of clinical experience, and/or not remaining current with the latest research - have become “experts” in various aspects of life including medicine, health and wellness. Is social media where one should go for medical advice?... So, if you have ANY questions about ANYTHING health-related, please make use of me and our RSM medical providers via our patient portal and the “Medical Questions” tab, therein. This provision is included in Charm (our health records keeping system that includes your “Patient Portal”) to facilitate our communicating between scheduled visits and to avoid potential deviations from optimizing health and unnecessary gnashing of teeth over something just researched, overheard at the gym, or published as “the latest discovery” through the media.

Make Your Goals and Commitment to Healthspan Commensurate with the Plan

Tangentially, the medical community likes to try to wrap up everything and everyone into a nice neat little package that makes it easy to generalize, but this can be a big mistake – especially if you don’t fit into ‘the average”. Sure, it often makes some sense to start with the most likely or average scenario, but this is only a start and often an approach that must be altered greatly depending upon the individual. E.g., amphetamine (aka “speed”) is a stimulant drug that when given to most people makes them more alert and ready to finally clean out the garage – twice! But, for roughly 10% of the U.S. population, amphetamine can initiate a calming effect – even somnolence (sleepiness)!

And, as another example, one of the longest-lived (117 years old) healthy individuals, Emme Morano, ignored the dietary advice of medical doctors and laypeople alike, and eschewed the consumption of vegetables and flourished eating mainly (raw) eggs. Finally, there are plenty of documented centenarians (people that live healthily to 100 years or more) that enjoy more than the CDC’s recommended “maximum” glasses of wine with dinner that have outlived their doctors!

Bottom line:

Make use of your medical Team at RSM to help you PERSONALLY and SPECIFICALLY combine your goals with the appropriate plan for YOU to achieve them.

Many of you are, like me, avid bicyclists or otherwise regularly actively exercising, and can appreciate how much fun it can be to be part of an athletic team or train with a partner. To that end, I encourage everyone to jump on “GarminConnect” or “Strava” with me to share workouts of all kinds and participate in the comradery. Your workouts (that can include all forms of exercise) will only be shared privately with me and mine with you, but you can link up with as many friends as you like on these platforms. I am listed as “Rand McClain” in “Malibu” on either site and if you log on and click “Follow” we can keep up with one another in our exercise endeavors.

Lastly, I would like to introduce you to a company in which I have invested and am a partner, Taste and Bliss (www.tasteandbliss.com).

Our first product is a delicious and chewy Coconut Cashew NutBar that I (and others) believe puts other “healthy” bars from Quaker Oats or any other brands to shame. That’s not where we stop. We'll be adding new flavors to the line as well as drink mixes, chocolates & more.

By the way, one of the goals of Taste & Bliss, and one reason for my interest in developing these products, is to give you the same taste experience that a typical sugar-filled snack or drink would give you but without the negative effects. This is made possible by the all-natural allulose* based functional sweetener my partners developed called NouveauSweet™. It acts, looks and tastes like sucrose (table sugar). (*Allulose is a naturally occurring rare sugar that comes from brown sugar, maple syrup, wheat, figs & raisins.)

I would appreciate your giving these bars a try and providing any feedback you have! And, in appreciation, I’ve asked my partners to provide a $10 credit towards your first order.

We will NOT be leaving behind our Santa Monica office (nor our home in Malibu)! We are simply planning on expanding to include an office in Miami, and will be dividing our time between these two locations. Consultation via telemedicine will continue to be offered per usual, but I will be less available for in-person consultation and procedures in Santa Monica.

Meanwhile, I would like to share some quick comments and interesting health news.

Methylene blue

‍has become a popular oral supplement touting legitimate benefits for mitochondrial health, neurocognitive function and protection, antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects, and mood enhancement. As with most supplements, using the appropriate dose is very important in order to enjoy the potential benefits and avoid the possible detrimental side effects. In general, while a dose of up to 3-4mg per kilogram of bodyweight can benefit mitochondrial, cognitive and psychological/mood function, a dose above 1-2mg per kilogram per day can decrease nitric oxide production, and, for most of us, that is something to avoid because of the potential benefits of maintaining nitric oxide production including significant all-cause mortality reduction.

‍Bottom line: if interested in using methylene blue, take no more than 2mg per kilogram per day, and, DO NOT take methylene blue if taking certain antidepressant drugs or serotonergic agents (SSRI’s, SNRI’s, MAO-inhibitors and Tramadol).

Estrogen

Estrogen in replacement therapy for women is crucial for many women and the recent removal of “Black Box Warnings” for women is long overdue and reflects recognition of a flaw in one of the most comprehensive and cited studies for woman conducted known as “The Women’s Health Initiative” (WHI).

MRI's

Full-body MRI’s and other imaging such as a coronary CT angiogram with and without contrast and NeuroQuant MRI are becoming popular tools for screening of issues that can be identified “early”, and therefore addressed and treated with a greater likelihood of success.

Genome mapping

Genome mapping once made little sense because there was little we could do to “treat” or control what our choice of parents did for us, and, the cost of mapping was over $10,000. Today, one can map one’s genome for less than $1,000, and can learn ways in which our genes affect our predilection for cancers and heart disease as well as other practical applications.

CellGym

This apparatus enables the use of Intermittent Hypoxic and Hyperoxic Therapy (IHHT) for a myriad of purposes to enhance health and fitness. While relaxing comfortably in a chair, one can breathe air manipulated to contain as little as 1/3 the partial pressure of oxygen at sea level or about the same effect as breathing at 5,000 meters (16,404 feet) of altitude followed by a mix of air containing and as much as 35% oxygen.

5-alpha reductase inhibitors

5-alpha reductase inhibitors (finasteride (Propecia and Proscar), dutasteride (Avodart), and saw palmetto) with nandrolone have long been discouraged citing the desire to allow nandrolone to convert to dihydronandrolone – a metabolite of nandrolone with much weaker androgenic effects (typically desired) than nandrolone itself. However, we now know that these aforementioned chemicals and the 5-alpha reductase inhibition have no effect on nandrolone and therefore can be employed concurrently for their intended effect to prevent testosterone from metabolizing into dihydrotestosterone – a strongly androgenic hormone that at various sufficient levels is responsible for initiating head hair loss, body and facial hair growth, acne, vocal cord thickening (voice deepening) and clitoral enlargement. Bottom line: you can take 5-alpha reductase inhibitors (finasteride (Propecia and Proscar), dutasteride (Avodart), and saw palmetto) to avoid potential negative side effects of dihydrotestosterone while also taking nandrolone.

Lastly, many of you did not receive the April newsletter that contained, among other items, information regarding blood thickness and stroke (“Thrombosis (blood clots), Blood Viscosity (“thickness”), and Testosterone”), and, for the men, testosterone and prostate cancer (“Testosterone & Prostate Cancer”). Please take a moment to read these as they dispel the very common misinformation circulating even amongst physicians.
